question.problem: Find the $17$th term of an arithmetic sequence if the $3$rd term is $-26$ and the $5$th term is $-12.$
question.worked_solution:
The formula for the $n$th term is given by

$$
{a}_{n}={a}_{1}+(n-1)d,
$$

 
so we need to figure out the first term ${a}_{1}$ and the common difference $d.$

To find the common difference, we can find the total difference between the terms ${a}_{3}=-26$ and ${a}_{5}=-12$ and divide it by the number of jumps, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =\frac{{a}_{5}-{a}_{3}}{5-3} \\  & =\frac{-12-(-26)}{5-3} \\  & =\frac{-12+26}{2} \\  & =\frac{14}{2} \\  & =7\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can use one of our known values, say, ${a}_{3}=-26,$ to determine the first term of the sequence. Since ${a}_{3}$ is $2$ jumps after ${a}_{1},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{3} & ={a}_{1}+2d \\ -26 & ={a}_{1}+2(7) \\ -26 & ={a}_{1}+14 \\ -26-14 & ={a}_{1} \\ {a}_{1} & =-40.\end{aligned}
$$

So the formula for the $n$th term is:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & =-40+(n-1)(7) \\  & =7n-47\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can find the $17$th term by substituting $n=17$ into the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{17} & =7(17)-47 \\  & =119-47 \\  & =72\end{aligned}
$$
